I'm currently a graphic designer with some web knowledge and am thinking about moving on. What are some good resources to get me started on a new path?

University pages. Seriously, go to like business-marketing or something and it will give you a list of possible career outcomes. From there you can read up on what that job entails through wiki, forums, linkedin, and payscale.

Edit: Payscale will also give you information pertaining to the average time people stay in that job, overlapping jobs (including experience), and career paths that you can follow to move on, or even branch out.

Can't think of any, but I'm happy to give my ill informed opinion.

I've changed my career field more than most. I was a journalist. I was an IT director. I was a game designer. I was a teacher. I was a consultant. Now I'm a distiller. Plenty of other jobs in between.

They say a key to living a good life is to have a job that makes you happy. In my mind, the way to find that job is to take whatever you do for fun, and find a way to make money off it. I was writing since I was a teen. Going into journalism was an extension of that urge. I was making games as a hobby. It made sense to become a game designer. I was volunteering for a community center teaching children computers. Of course I would become a teacher. I was passionate about helping the local start up community. Consulting was a logical step. I had been making booze out of my garage for years and years. Distiller is a good fit.

Point is, I didn't start working and learned to love my job. Instead I took the things I loved, and made them jobs. I didn't care about pay, since these were things I would be doing anyways.

I'm at work right now. It's two in the morning. I couldn't sleep, so I came in a few hours early simply because I love what I do.

So here's the best resource you have. Yourself. What are your hobbies? Let's find some jobs that would fit.

Go get some help. (ie. Therapy). The only way "out" (of bad feelings) is "through" (allow yourself to FEEL them).

If you have anxiety, insomnia, and hair pulling, then the traditional psychological view of these issues is that these are all coping mechanisms to help you avoid feeling these bad feelings. Often, you're just going to need to talk it out with a unimpassioned third-party, who has no stake in the game, no agenda, no alliances or allegiances, no past hurts. . . etc. that's what a therapist is, that's what they do, and that's what they're for. A good therapist can really help with these things. I'm going to go out on a limb and say that the TYPE of therapy that can help you, is probably CBT and DBT (cognitive behavioral therapy, and dialectical behavioral therapy).

You will probably get NO help from your parents (given the situation you've described), so this is something you have to do on your own. You may need to go through their insurance to pay - but there are also programs out there, for kids, who can get help paying. If your parents want to cooperate, enthusiastically, see if they'll do group. But if they show any signs of reluctance, it can probably do more harm than good.

Also; try to avoid alcohol and drugs, as a coping mechanism. (particularly, try to avoid typical anti-anxiety medications like valium, ativan, xanax, and especially klonopin - a lot of crisis situations will get people started on one of these for acute anxiety, and they are highly addictive, and have terrible come-down effects for people suffering from anxiety).

I am personally, all for the legalization of soft drugs, (like mj), for medical and recreational use. But people who are struggling with these kinds of issues should AVOID drugs and self-medicating, because they quickly become a coping mechanism for tuning out and covering up, and prevent people from dealing with their feelings, and worse, give them a tool to avoid dealing with difficult life situations in a healthy way. It doesn't take long for someone at your age, to permanently ruin chances at a happy, and successful future, by tuning out from classes, jobs, sports, and other healthy activities.

Finally, begin to plan. Plan a future; two years from now, when you are 18. Plan an escape. Plan what you're going to do with your life to get out of this abusive situation, get out on your own, support yourself, and take care of your own needs without being reliant on abusive assholes.
